tagline: Up the razor-clam beaches to the Quinault River.
intro: SR 109 leaves Hoquiam along Bowerman Basin and the Grays Harbor wildlife refuge, climbs onto Brackenridge Bluff, and comes around the north side of the harbor past cranberry bogs. At Ocean City it turns north and keeps to the Pacific as far as Copalis Beach, where centuries-old stumps of a ghost forest come up out of the sand. Then it runs on through Pacific Beach and Moclips.

North of the Moclips River it enters the Quinault Indian Reservation, comes down onto the beach along Grenville Bay and ends at Taholah, at the south end of the Quinault River bridge. Plans to carry it on up the coast to Queets go back to the mid-20th century.

moments.title: Copalis Beach
moments.text: Known as the Home of the razor clam, its beach gave up more than a million pounds of them to commercial diggers in 1947 and 1948.

moments.title: Moclips
moments.text: Edward Lycan's Moclips Beach Hotel of 1907 ran a block long behind 2,000 feet of covered veranda, and after the storms of 1911 there was nothing left of it by 1913.

moments.title: Taholah
moments.text: Named in 1905 for a Quinault chief, the village keeps a 2,000-foot seawall against the ocean and in 2021 opened the first building of a new village uphill.

sources.label: State of Washington Tourism, Hidden Coast Scenic Byway
